wall_families.castle-rough: NEW: wall-straight (2), wall-window-small = arrow slit, wall-doorway, portcullis (+raised), city-wall (+turret) for the courtyard edge
wall_families.dressed-stone: EXISTS (wall-straight x2, wall-window-small, wall-doorway, corners, doors): used for great hall, throne room, chapel; NEW window-stained-glass--dressed-stone panel

doors.door-reinforced--leaf: NEW leaf-only (rotates): the castle's default door
doors.door-double-grand--leaf: EXISTS: hall, throne room, chapel main door
doors.door-cell-bars: NEW cell-front panel with a barred door (+open twin)

rooms.label: Great hall
rooms.reads_by: the huge hooded fireplace on one wall + the long high table on a dais across the top end + two rows of trestle tables with benches down the hall

doors.main: door-double-grand (leaf exists) in the short wall opposite the dais

must: fireplace-grand centred on a LONG wall (the hearth pole), 6 ft working face kept clear

dais against the short wall facing the main door; table-feast ON the dais, parallel to that wall, chair-armed--high-seat centred behind it (back to the wall) with 2-6 chair-armed either side, nobody seated on the hall side
program.rows: table-trestle end to end in 2 rows (3 from 40 ft wide) running the long axis from the dais toward the door, bench-long both sides, a 6-ft centre aisle; one row only under 25 ft wide
walls: heraldic-shield over or beside the fireplace
banner-wall / tapestry flats on the long walls, one per 10 ft
shield-display, trophy-head
torch-bracket-fine every 10-15 ft
centre: chandelier-ring--great over the centre aisle, one per 25 ft of hall
brazier-large in the centre aisle only if there is no fireplace wall free
program.on_things: high table: cas-high-table-setting + cas-feast-spread smalls (salt-cellar-ship in the middle, goblet-silver, platter-silver, boar-head-platter, candelabra); trestles: common tableware
program.counts: per 100 sq ft target 6; pillar-round in two rows 10 ft in from the long walls from 40 ft wide; banner-pole pair flanking the dais; armor-stand pair by the main door

rooms.label: Throne room
rooms.reads_by: the throne on its dais at the far end + a red runner straight from the door to it + a symmetric avenue of pillars, braziers and armour stands

doors.main: door-double-grand in the short wall facing the throne (the one room where the door IS in line with the focal piece)

must: dais axial focal (ROOMS.md Principle 8): centred on the wall facing the main door, flanked symmetrically; throne ON the dais, centred, facing the door; dais--s2 (one step, 9 ft square) when the wall is under 14 ft
centre: rug-runner--royal (flat) laid end to end from the door to the dais foot: the processional line, 5 ft wide, kept clear of everything
program.rows: an avenue either side of the runner, mirrored left/right, repeating every 10 ft from the dais toward the door: pillar-round, then brazier-large or brazier-standing, then armor-stand (facing the runner)
walls: banner-pole one each side of the throne on the dais or at its foot
banner-wall flats behind the throne and down both long walls
window-stained-glass--dressed-stone panels in the long walls (wall kit)
heraldic-shield above the throne
program.extras: faldstool x2-4 at the dais foot to one side (courtiers); chest-treasure and regalia-cushion on a table-side by the dais in big rooms; crown and scepter are loot smalls on the regalia table
program.counts: per 100 sq ft target 3.5 (formal and open); nothing but the runner on the centre line

rooms.label: Armoury
rooms.reads_by: weapon racks shoulder to shoulder along the walls + armour stands in ranks on the floor + the grindstone and repair bench by the door

must: weapon-rack (3 shapes) is the wall-rack item: fills every free wall run, one per 5 ft, shapes alternating; the tall polearm rack (s2) on the wall facing the door
program.rows: armor-stand (3 shapes) is the aisle-row item from 20x20 ft: ranks of stands 4 ft apart, all facing the door, 4-ft aisles; under that, 2-4 stands in the corners
walls: mil-crossbow-rack and smith-helm-row-shelf hung above / between racks
heraldic-shield--s2 over the door
program.by_door: grindstone + mil-armor-repair-bench (the tally-desk slot), arrow-barrel pair, mil-shield-stack, chest-ironbound
program.on_things: repair bench and chests carry cas-armory-smalls and loose arms: helm-great, helm-open, armor-breastplate, crossbow, sword-short, axe-hand, mace-flanged, warhammer, quiver-arrows; shields lean at rack ends
program.counts: floor coverage about 25% like the storeroom

rooms.label: Barracks / guard room
rooms.reads_by: rows of bunk beds each with a footlocker at its foot + a guard table with dice and mugs by the door + helmets and weapons on the wall

must: the dormitory branch at EVERY size: bunk-bed is the bed (never the axial single bed), head to the wall, one per 5 ft along both long walls; mil-footlocker at each bunk's foot (the foot-chest slot)
program.rows: middle rows head-to-head from 600 sq ft, as the guest dormitory; cot fills odd gaps
program.by_door: the guard-room zone: table-square + bench-long / stool-three-leg, dice-and-cup, tankard, mil-guard-lantern on the table; weapon-rack--s1 and armor-stand--s2 beside the door; brazier-tripod near the table
walls: mil-helmet-peg-rack between bunks (the coat-pegs slot)
mil-duty-roster and horn-hunting by the door
smith-helm-row-shelf
program.counts: per 100 sq ft target 8 as the dormitory; 12 bunks in the default 30x20

rooms.label: Castle kitchen
rooms.reads_by: the 11-ft great hearth with its spit filling one wall + the cauldron on its crane in the middle + the bread oven and long work tables

must: the industrial-kitchen branch from the default size up; the FIRST cooking line is cook-hearth-spit--great (11 ft, centred on a long wall, working face 6 ft), further lines use the existing cook-hearth-spit skus
centre: cauldron-crane in the open middle in front of the great hearth (one; a second from 1,500 sq ft)
cauldron-huge and pig-on-spit as row end caps
program.rows: table-kitchen-prep--great end to end as the work rows (existing prep tables and butcher-block as segments)
walls: bread-oven bake corner as built (peel, bread-rack, flour)
larder runs as built
basin-stone scullery
program.overhead: trade-butcher-hooks-rail hangs over the aisles with ham-hanging, kettle-hanging (ceiling)
program.on_things: saucepan-copper, fish-kettle, pot-copper on tables and the hearth kerb; mortar-large-stone on the floor at a table end
program.counts: per 100 sq ft target 10 as the kitchen

rooms.label: Castle chapel
rooms.reads_by: the altar on a step at the far end + rows of pews facing it either side of a centre aisle + stained-glass windows and tall candle stands

doors.main: door-double-grand in the short wall facing the altar

must: dais--s2 axial focal (ROOMS.md Principle 8): centred on the wall facing the main door, flanked symmetrically; altar-stone ON it, long side to the room, 3 ft off the wall; candelabra-standing--iron one each side of the altar
program.rows: pew (3 shapes) is the aisle-row item: rows across the room all FACING the altar, 3 ft apart front to back, in two blocks either side of a 5-ft centre aisle (one block against a wall under 15 ft wide); the front row 8 ft from the dais; pew--s3 (short) fills narrow blocks
walls: window-stained-glass--dressed-stone panels in the long walls (wall kit), one per 10 ft, never on the door wall
sconce-candle-triple between windows
program.by_door: font-holy just inside the door to one side; prayer-candle-rack against the wall on the other
program.extras: lectern at the dais foot, off the centre line, turned to the pews; rite-altar-emblem-stand behind the altar; rite-kneeler-cushion in front of the altar
program.on_things: altar: chalice-altar, tome-holy, reliquary, candlestick pair (tem-altar-service)
program.shared_with: the crypt's chapel of rest uses the same ids: altar-stone, reliquary come from the crypt batch; pew, lectern, font-holy, prayer-candle-rack, candelabra-standing--iron, chalice-altar, tome-holy from this one

rooms.label: Dungeon
rooms.reads_by: a row of barred cells along one wall (bar fronts, a barred door each, a plank bed inside) + the rack in the open floor + the iron maiden and brazier of irons against the far wall

must: cells are the stalls: 5 or 10 ft wide x 10 ft deep along ONE long wall; partitions between cells are wall-straight--castle-rough (full height); each cell front is cell-bars panels with exactly one door-cell-bars panel; one cell in five rolls its door open (door-cell-bars-open)
program.in_cell: cell-bench-plank hung on a side wall (or bed-straw-pallet on the floor), bucket-slop, manacles-wall on the back wall, rug-hay-scatter; one cell in six: bones-pile instead of a bed
centre: the aisle in front of the cells stays clear 5 ft; in the open half: rack-torture (long axis along the room), table-experiment from 600 sq ft
walls: iron-maiden axial focal (ROOMS.md Principle 8): centred on the wall facing the main door, flanked symmetrically when there is a free wall facing the door, else in a far corner; one in three open (iron-maiden-open)
brazier-irons beside the rack
stocks / pillory / cage-floor / block-headsman along the far wall, one each as the room grows
lever-wall and key-hook-board by the door (jailer station: table-square, stool, mil-guard-lantern)
program.floor: oubliette-hatch in a far corner (one, from 500 sq ft); floor-drain-grate and decal-blood flats near the rack
program.small: under 300 sq ft: no cells; rack + iron maiden + brazier-irons only (a torture chamber)
program.counts: per 100 sq ft target 4; dark: 1 light per 250 sq ft

rooms.label: Gatehouse
rooms.reads_by: the portcullis arch in the outer wall and a clear cart-wide passage straight through + the windlass with its chain beside it + guard kit (spear tripod, crossbow rack, brazier, sentry box)

doors.main: portcullis--castle-rough: a TWO-cell gate panel on the outside wall (raised twin = open state)
doors.others: a second portcullis or door-reinforced--leaf on the opposite wall, toward the courtyard: a passageway on purpose

must: the through-line gate to gate, 10 ft wide, kept completely clear (carts)
windlass against the wall beside the outer gate, lever-wall on the wall above/beside it
walls: wall-window-small--castle-rough (arrow slits) on the OUTSIDE wall either side of the gate
weapon-rack--s2 (polearms), mil-crossbow-rack, mil-helmet-peg-rack, horn-hunting, mil-duty-roster
program.sides: in the bands either side of the passage: guard table (table-square, bench-long, dice, mil-guard-lantern), brazier-large or fire-basket-stand, mil-spear-tripod, arrow-barrel, mil-pavise, armor-stand--s2/s3; mil-boiling-oil-pot in a corner by the outer gate from 20x20; oubliette-hatch reads as a murder hole in big ones
program.outside: when a courtyard or yard adjoins: sentry-box, banner-pole--s2 and watch-lantern-bell just outside the gate (placed by the courtyard)
program.counts: per 100 sq ft target 4; nothing in the passage

rooms.label: Courtyard
rooms.reads_by: a battlemented curtain wall with corner turrets and a gate round cobbles + the well in the open + a training corner (dummies, archery butts, a rack of practice swords)

program.same_as_yard: walls.js outdoor role unchanged: no walls of its own, ground instead of floor, neighbours' doors open onto it, paths door -> gate reserved first, sparse (2 per 100 sq ft)
program.edge: ALWAYS enclosed (no 'none' roll): city-wall--castle-rough on every open grid edge (box 60x30x132, on the grid line, thick like the hedge: the strip it covers is blocked); city-wall-turret--castle-rough where a run ends or turns (not where it meets a building); the gate piece is portcullis--castle-rough (two cells) on the gate's segment, rolled 1 in 3 gate-double-timber leaves between two turrets instead
program.focal: one in the open, clear of the door-to-gate line: the well (existing mesh) 2 in 3; else horse-trough-stone, or cauldron-crane / pig-on-spit (feast day)
program.training_corner: from 900 sq ft, in the corner farthest from the gate, on a patch of floor-sand-training: 2-3 training-dummy (s1/s2) and mil-pell in a line 6 ft apart; archery-target (s1/s2) x2 against the curtain wall with 30 ft of clear range in front; mil-wasters-rack, weapon-rack--s2, arrow-barrel, mil-shield-stack at the wall; tourney-lists-rail sections fencing the patch's open side; mil-quintain from 2,000 sq ft
program.by_gate: sentry-box, watch-lantern-bell, banner-pole, brazier-large or mil-signal-beacon; mil-cheval-de-frise and mil-pavise stacked aside; ballista near the gate from 1,500 sq ft
program.by_doors: kitchen door: woodpile, barrels, crates as the inn yard; stable door: trough, hay, hitching-post as the inn yard; hall door: torch-stand pair, banner-pole pair; chapel door: nothing but a torch
program.at_wall: stone-blocks-stack, mil-catapult-stones, grindstone, sawhorse, stocks (and block-headsman 1 in 8) against the curtain wall; wagon / cart-hand as the inn yard
program.no: no plants slot (bare military court), no fences or hedges, no inn sign, no kennel, no washing line
